newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN CASH DEFICIT 9-1/2 BLN MARKS IN JULY - BUBA.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN CASH DEFICIT 9-1/2 BLN MARKS IN JULY - BUBA.

text.p: The German federal government's cash deficit totalled about 9-1/2 billion marks in July, around 2-1/2 billion marks above the level in the same month in 1996, the Bundesbank said in its August monthly report.
The Bundesbank said this marked a break from a trend towards an improving cash position seen in recent months.
"In total the deficit for the first seven months ran at about 60 billion marks and so exceeded the comparable amount from the previous year by 15 billion marks," it said.
"While cash income rose by 4.8 percent, outgoings showed a rise of 4.8 percent," it said.
But it cautioned that the figures could well be very different from Bonn's overall budget figures and could not be extrapolated to predict the likely budget outlook for the year.
Income from planned privatisations, for example, would not be booked until much later in the year, it said.

Turning to net new debt, the Bundesbank said there had been a reduction of debt in June, noting that it was a heavy tax-receipt month. Total German public authority debt was reduced by 7-1/2 billion marks and federal debt by two billion.
Borrowing of 10-1/2 billion marks in capital markets was offset by a reduction in money market borrowing of 12-1/2 billion marks. German states also cut their debt position by six billion marks.
Total net borrowing for German public authorities was 56 billion marks in the first half of 1997, the Bundesbank said. This was an increase of 25 billion marks from a year ago.

In July, the federal government took up a gross total of 24-1/2 billion marks of funds from capital markets but paid off 27-1/2 billion marks of debt, leaving a net reduction of three billion marks in its overall debt position.
But its borrowing in the German money market increased by almost 15 billion marks, the Bundesbank said. --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
